terms.comment: An ordinary description, stuffed with cream: cremum (Traupman 71) and fartus, the participle of farciō, to stuff (Cic., Plin., in Lewis & Short). Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no single word; Morgan–Owens gives Apicius’s farsilis for stuffed.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 71.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. stuffed.
